messages.author: d9e6fc961c414390
messages.subject: INLA SPDE Informative Priors
parts:
Hi,

I have two datasets with spde effects. What I'm trying to do is run the model on one dataset and use the result as the prior for the other dataset (i.e. informative prior). I want to ask for advice on which parameters should I use. 

For the fixed effects, I basically used the result$summary.fixed mean and standard deviation, which is simple enough. But I'm not sure about the hyperparameters for the SPDE. My code is as below.


spde.result <- inla.spde.result(result, "spatial", spde)

spde2 <- inla.spde2.matern(mesh = mesh,
                            alpha = 2, 
                            prior.variance.nominal = spde.result$summary.log.variance.nominal$mean,
                            prior.range.nominal = spde.result$summary.log.range.nominal$mean
                            #, prior.tau = spde.result$summary.log.tau$mean, 
                            # prior.kappa = spde.result$summary.log.kappa$mean
                            )

Which should I specify and what's the difference between 
- prior.variance.nominal vs prior.tau
- prior.range.nominal vs prior.kappa

and am I doing it correctly taking the summary.log._$mean as it is, or do I need to transform them using exp()?


Any advice is appreciated. Thanks!

messages.author: d9e6fc961c414390
messages.subject: Re: INLA SPDE Informative Priors
parts: In addition to my query above, should I do posterior sampling first, and use that result instead or just using the fitted model is good enough as informative priors?

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] INLA SPDE Informative Priors
parts:
Hi,

LogTau and logkappa are the internal parameters, so specifying the priors for those is the most direct way to transfer information from a previous run. Your commented out lines should do exactly that. The nominal variance and range are theoretically derived quantities, that assume no boundary effects etc, so aren’t appropriate for use in this context.

You’ll also need to specify the prior precisions; ideally, that would include an entire joint precision matrix, but that would take some effort to extract from the joint posterior covariance for all the hyperparameters in your model, but is should be possible. Alternatively, you can specify the prior precision by hand, using only the previous posterior means as new prior means.

Finn

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] INLA SPDE Informative Priors
parts:
I,

The marginals structure stores the marginal density functions, so aren’t useful to get the covariance. That is stored elsewhere; I’m not at a computer to check precisely where, but possibly in $misc of the inla result object.

For just the marginal precisions, then yes, 1/sd^2 is the right thing.

Finn
